project.name: MediRec
project.description: MediRec connects verified Canadian healthcare workers with facilities for shift staffing, with agency (partner) support. Built on React, Vite and Supabase, hosted on Vercel, with data in Canada (ca-central-1). This dashboard tracks progress and is auto-updated from the MediRec.ca WhatsApp group.

milestones.title: Migration plan + rollback checkpoint
milestones.detail: Written migration plan (schema, data, auth, storage, functions, secrets), hosting confirmation, tagged rollback release and procedure.

milestones.title: Migrate to ca-central-1 (Canada)
milestones.detail: All tables, auth users, storage and functions in the Canadian project; RLS verified; core flows passing.

milestones.title: Priority defects
milestones.detail: Commission timezone (done), facility signup role, role-based permissions, 'Account not configured', full-app refetch on tab switch.

milestones.title: Security review + handover
milestones.detail: Review SECURITY DEFINER views, written findings, handover, certificate of deletion.

milestones.title: Five-star reviews
milestones.detail: Facility and worker rate each other after a completed shift; public stars, private comments, Play-Store-style breakdown on profiles.

milestones.title: Profiles as full pages
milestones.detail: Worker and facility profiles open as clean, no-index pages instead of popups everywhere.

milestones.title: Designated-worker invite
milestones.detail: Admin and agency can send an open shift straight to a specific verified worker.

milestones.title: Final approval on matched worker
milestones.detail: Facility + agency approval gate built; workflow being adjusted to agency then MediRec final approval per client.

milestones.title: Admin tooling
milestones.detail: Create users with a chosen password, delete workers/facilities, and mark a worker verified from the dashboard.

achievements: Two-way five-star reviews with private comments and a rating breakdown on profiles.
Worker and facility profiles converted from popups to clean, no-index pages.
Designated-worker invite for admin and agency, with permission rules.
Final approval gate for matched shifts (facility + agency); workflow refinement in progress.
Admin can create a user with a set password, delete accounts, and verify a worker directly.
Table/card view toggles and mobile-responsive admin pages.
Automatic cleanup of stale, unfilled, past-dated shifts.
GitHub Action to auto-deploy database migrations and edge functions.
Fixed the '0 users' count, the Create User errors, and the invite button hang.

daily.summary: We shipped the two way reviews, turned the worker and facility profiles into clean pages, and added the designated worker invite so an open shift can go straight to a chosen worker. We also built the final approval step for a matched shift, and gave admin the tools to create a user with a set password, verify a worker, and delete accounts. On the side we set up the WhatsApp summary bot and this dashboard. The approval flow will move to agency then MediRec once the client confirms.

Asad hit an error while creating an account and suggested making the facility sign up smoother. He and Hammad went over admin access, being able to see shifts in different views, and tagging workers the right way. They also talked through how shift approvals should flow and whether MediRec itself should sit in the approval step, and Hammad asked whether facilities could use MediRec internally for their own scheduling and payroll. The other big topic was moving the Supabase database from the US to Canada and connecting that new database to the site on Vercel, and Asad shared a Trello board so everyone can follow progress.

On decisions, Hammad wants to keep the current setup rather than rebuild the app, so the plan is to move the existing app to Vercel and keep making changes on top of it. Asad will give the app a visual rebrand so the important information is clearer and better aligned. Hammad will also make a small change in Lovable and publish it, just to check that nothing breaks once the Canadian database is connected.

A few things are still open. Asad needs to run a query to see if the password hashes are present in the Supabase database, and Hammad needs to hand over the data that will go into the new Canadian database. They still need to agree on the cutover checklist, including the freeze window, syncing the worker uploads, and what happens to logins at the moment of the switch. Asad will also list the 7 accounts that have no password and break the 64 users down by role so we know the real worker count. Hammad wants to confirm that Lovable still works normally against the Canadian database before going any further.

weekly.summary: This week we cleared the admin tooling problems, so the user count is right again and creating, verifying, and deleting users all work. We added the two way reviews and the new profile pages, and we built the two agency features, the designated worker invite and the final approval on a matched shift. We also set up automatic deploys for the database and functions, and a bot that summarizes the WhatsApp group into this dashboard. The approval flow is being finalized with the client.
